name: MCBR-RAG (A General Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework for Multimodal Case-Based Reasoning Applications)
venue: arXiv preprint (arXiv:2501.05030 [cs.AI]; also cross-listed cs.CL), submitted 9 Jan 2025. No peer-reviewed venue identified as of the search date; 15 pages, 7 figures. DBLP records it as journals/corr/abs-2501-05030 (arXiv/CoRR), DOI 10.48550/arXiv.2501.05030.
authors_affiliation: Ofir Marom (sole author), Independent Researcher (ofiremarom@gmail.com). Acknowledges Prof. Benjamin Rosman (University of the Witwatersrand) for discussions, but Rosman is not a co-author.
code_url: https://github.com/OfirMarom/Math24 (official; Python implementation of the Math-24 application only -- pipeline/, experiments/, processing/, llm_api.py, solutions.csv; initial commit 26 Dec 2024). The Backgammon application code/data is NOT released.
maintained_repo_url: N/A (single-application demo repo above is the only artifact; no leaderboard or maintained paper-list).
task_domain: Decision-making / problem-solving framed as multimodal case-based reasoning. Two demonstrator applications: (1) Math-24 puzzle solving (text+image; arithmetic reasoning) and (2) Backgammon move analysis (text+image; game-playing expert commentary generation). Both are knowledge-intensive generation tasks where the case problem has non-text (image) components.
problem_setting: Offline, single-agent, non-interactive RAG over a fixed case repository, generalized to MULTIMODAL cases. A case is a tuple C=(P,S,R) where the problem P=(p_1,...,p_n) has components of arbitrary modality (e.g., image), the solution S is text, and R is the result/outcome. A general framework (MCBR-RAG) converts each non-text problem component into (a) a text-based representation (for LLM context) and (b) a learned application-specific latent representation (for retrieval indexing). At inference: given a new case problem P~, retrieve the top-k most similar solved cases via weighted-average cosine similarity over per-component latent representations, then build an augmented query containing the textified problem + retrieved (textified) cases and prompt a frozen LLM to generate the solution. Supervision: application-specific text-generation models (CNNs) and latent-representation models (FFNNs) are trained on synthetic/labeled data (40,000 Math-24 card images; 100,000 simulated Backgammon board images; GNU Backgammon value labels); the generator LLM is off-the-shelf and frozen. The framework explicitly covers only the Retrieve and Reuse CBR phases; Revise and Retain are left application-specific and not implemented in the experiments.
what_is_retrieved: cases (problem-solution-result tuples). For Math-24: prior solved puzzle cases (card image -> solution set). For Backgammon: prior solved lesson cases (board position image + player + dice + move -> expert textual analysis). Retrieved cases supply both a precise execution plan/strategy (Math-24) and expert analysis exemplars (Backgammon) as LLM context.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus / case repository. The repository is built offline from curated sources (466 Math-24 puzzles in the chosen solution form; 1015 Backgammon cases collected from three expert books) and is frozen at inference time -- no episodic write-back during the experiments. (The CBR Retain phase that would grow the store is acknowledged but deliberately left out of the general framework / experiments.)
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k ranking objective: retrieval returns the arg-top_k most similar cases by a weighted-average cosine similarity (Eq. 7). Math-24 generation uses the single Top Context (TC, k=1) case; Backgammon generation uses the top-3 (k=3) most similar cases. Retrieval quality is reported as Precision@k/Recall@k/F1@k/NDCG@k/MRR@k averaged over k in {1,2,3,4,5}. It is a ranking/relevance objective, not minimal-set completeness or a precision-driven variable-size recommendation.
cbr_cycle_coverage: [Retrieve, Reuse, -, -] -- the framework explicitly implements only the Retrieve (RAG retrieval, Eq. 7) and Reuse (RAG generation, Eq. 8) phases. Revise (Eq. 3) and Retain (Eq. 4) are formalized in the CBR background but stated to be application-specific and NOT handled generally (the paper notes DS-Agent could implement Revise/Retain via test-set evaluation, but MCBR-RAG itself does not).
explicit_cbr_grounding: True. The work explicitly frames itself as Case-Based Reasoning, defines the four-phase CBR pipeline (Retrieve/Reuse/Revise/Retain), and cites the canonical CBR foundations Aamodt & Plaza (1994) and Gilboa & Schmeidler's case-based decision theory (1995). It positions RAG as supporting the Retrieve and Reuse CBR stages and cites prior LLM-CBR works (CBR-RAG, CaseGPT, DS-Agent, logical-fallacy CBR).
retrieval_unit: case (problem-solution-result tuple). The query key is the new-case problem P~ converted to per-component latent representations; the retrieved payload is the full solved case (problem textified + solution S + result R). For Backgammon a case = (board-position image z, player p, dice r, move m, expert analysis S, accuracy R); for Math-24 a case = (card image P, solution set S, results R).
index_source: Static, offline-induced repository. Math-24: 466 puzzles (subset of 1362 solvable puzzles restricted to the (x1 o x2) x (x3 o x4)=24 form). Backgammon: 1015 cases collected from three expert books (Magriel 'Backgammon' 1977/X-22; Robertie '501 Essential Backgammon Problems'; Trice 'Backgammon Bootcamp'); ~90% retention after legality validation of CNN-extracted positions. No online/test-time induction; the store is frozen.
index_structure_topology: Flat vector index with per-component (multi-field) embeddings. Each case is indexed by application-specific learned latent vectors (64-unit FFNN embeddings). Retrieval is kNN over a WEIGHTED AVERAGE of per-component cosine similarities (Eq. 7, sum_j w_j CosineSim(L_j(p~_j), L_j(p_{i,j})), weights >0 summing to 1). For Backgammon the latent key averages the position latent and the post-move position latent ( (l_z + l_z')/2 ). No graph/hierarchical/cluster topology.
retriever_type: Dense (learned-embedding kNN). Retrieval uses cosine similarity over application-specific latent representations produced by trained FFNNs (Math-24: multi-label classifier FFNN; Backgammon: multi-task FFNN with a value head + a decoder/reconstruction head). No BM25/sparse, no LLM-as-retriever, no generative tool-as-token retrieval. A 'Features'/'Encoding' baseline uses hand-crafted/raw-encoding cosine similarity instead of the learned latent.
retriever_learning_signal: Learned, but via SUPERVISED PROXY tasks rather than retrieval/contrastive labels or downstream LLM feedback. Math-24: the latent FFNN is trained as a multi-label classification task predicting solution category + decomposition (40 engineered features + 4 puzzle numbers as input, 4x5 sigmoid outputs), so the embedding clusters puzzles with similar solution structure. Backgammon: the latent FFNN is trained multi-task to predict (a) position value (win/loss probability, from GNU Backgammon labels) and (b) reconstruct the encoded position (decoder), so the embedding captures both strategic value and checker configuration. There is no contrastive similarity-label training, no LM-feedback, no RL, and the retrieval weights w_j (Math-24) / value-vs-decoder weights (Backgammon, swept e.g. (1,0.01)) are hand-tuned/grid-searched, not learned end-to-end.
query_construction: Raw new-case problem converted by application-specific functions. For retrieval: each problem component p~_j is mapped to its latent representation L_j(p~_j) (image -> text via CNN text-generator -> latent FFNN). For generation: the textified problem T(P~) plus the textified top-k retrieved cases T(C_k) are assembled into an augmented query q_RAG=Query(T(P~), T(C_k)). Math-24 uses a fixed parsing-convention system prompt; for the Top Context query the retrieved case is converted into a precise step-by-step execution plan (solution category + decomposition). No query decomposition into sub-queries.
query_granularity: Task-level (one-shot at t=0): a single retrieval per new case, with the whole (multimodal) problem as the query, followed by a single conditioned generation. No per-step or trajectory-level re-retrieval. (Backgammon optionally averages two related latent vectors -- current and post-move position -- but this is still one retrieval per case.)
when_to_retrieve: One-shot: retrieval is performed once per new case before generation (retrieve-then-generate). No iterative/active/adaptive re-retrieval.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule: retrieval always occurs once per incoming case at the start of the Reuse/generation pipeline. The No Context (NC) baseline simply skips retrieval; the General Context (GC, Math-24) baseline injects a fixed generic tip instead of a retrieved case. No confidence/uncertainty/learned-router/reflection trigger.
reranking: None. The arg-top_k cases by weighted-average cosine similarity are passed directly to the generator. The Backgammon similarity-weight sweep ((value, decoder) weights such as (1,0.01) chosen as best) is a tuning of the single-stage similarity score, not a second-stage reranker. No cross-encoder/RRF/instruction-tuned reranking.
retrieved_context_refinement: Minimal / selection + reformatting only. Math-24: the single top case (TC) is reformatted into an explicit step-by-step execution plan (solution category + decomposition) before injection; the GC variant injects a generic tip rather than a retrieved case. Backgammon: the top-3 cases are injected verbatim as (position JSON, player, dice, move, expert analysis). There is no decompose-recompose, distillation across multiple cases, distractor filtering, or compression. A legality-validation filter discards ~10% of Backgammon cases, but that happens during offline index construction, not post-retrieval.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (no tools/APIs; retrieved units are CBR cases, not tool documents). The closest analogue is the bespoke text-generation pipeline (CNNs) that converts image components into text strings for both indexing-input and context, and the engineered aggregate features (Math-24's 40 pair-counting features) feeding the latent model.
index_content_separation: Partial: lightweight learned latent vectors (the retrieval index) are separated from the heavier full case content (textified problem + solution + analysis) that is loaded into the prompt only after the kNN match. This mirrors CBR's index-vs-content separation but is not an agentic progressive-disclosure / SOP-index-then-content mechanism.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (no tool index / external API protocol; static case repository, no CRUD auto-sync / RapidAPI / MCP / function-calling).
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A (no tools; no inter-tool dependency modeling).
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation / case reuse: the textified top-k retrieved cases are concatenated into the LLM query as additional context (q_RAG=Query(T(P~), T(C_k))), and a frozen LLM generates the solution S~=L(q_RAG) (Eq. 8). For Math-24 the retrieved case is converted into an explicit execution plan the LLM follows; for Backgammon the retrieved analyses serve as exemplars to imitate. Adaptation is implicit/LLM-internal -- there is no explicit case-revision step.
planning_integration: Retrieve-then-generate (one-shot exemplars at generation time). Retrieval happens once up front; the k retrieved cases condition a single answer/analysis generation. There is no multi-step planning loop, tree search, or per-step interleaving. For Math-24, the retrieved case essentially supplies a one-shot solution plan (use pair to make {1,24}/{2,12}/{3,8}/{4,6} then multiply) that the LLM executes in a single pass.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-answer / per-case: a single retrieval feeds a single conditioned generation producing one solution/analysis per new case. Retrieval is not woven per CoT-step or per token.
adaptation_mechanism: LLM-prompted adaptation (implicit). Retrieved cases are injected as context and the frozen LLM reuses/adapts their solutions when generating the new solution; for Math-24 the retrieved case is templated into an execution plan that the LLM applies to the new puzzle. There is no explicit CBR Revise step (no execution-feedback revision, critic-guided revision, or RL reuse-finetuning) -- Revise is explicitly left application-specific and unimplemented.
retrieved_item_representation: Textified case content injected into the prompt. Math-24: a step-by-step execution-plan tip derived from the retrieved case's solution category + decomposition (or a generic tip for GC). Backgammon: the retrieved cases' position (JSON-encoded), player, dice, move, plus the expert free-text analysis. Underlying images are first converted to text strings (e.g., '4 5 9 10' for Math-24; '1X2 2X3 3O2 ...' for Backgammon). No latent-soft tokens or executable programs are injected.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Single demonstration / case at the problem-solution level, with light strategy abstraction. Backgammon retrieves literal prior solved cases (board + expert analysis) as exemplars. Math-24 retrieves a single case but presents it as a distilled, state-aware execution plan (solution category + decomposition strategy) rather than a verbatim worked example. Not a reusable workflow library or procedural skill.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Limited / representation-level + filtering. (1) Application-specific learned latent spaces (multi-label-classification FFNN for Math-24; value+decoder multi-task FFNN for Backgammon) are designed so retrieved cases share solution structure / strategic value, improving relevance over raw features (latent similarity beats feature similarity on all metrics). (2) Offline legality validation discards ~10% of Backgammon cases whose CNN-extracted positions are illegal. (3) Backgammon excludes from retrieval all cases originating from the same source analysis as the test case (anti-leakage). There is NO per-retrieval relevance evaluator, self-reflection, reason-in-documents refinement, or distractor-aware training; the paper notes that incorrect context can mislead the LLM (low Negative Rejection on Math-24).
memory_type: none (static case repository used for retrieval only). It is a non-parametric CBR case store, not an episodic/skill/workflow memory that grows or self-updates during deployment.
write_back: False -- the implemented framework does not store newly solved cases back into the repository at inference. The CBR Retain phase (Eq. 4) is formalized but explicitly left application-specific and not realized in the experiments.
online_growth: No -- the repository is frozen after offline construction (466 Math-24 cases; 1015 Backgammon cases) and does not grow at deployment/test time.
write_back_trigger: Never -- no write-back is implemented (Retain phase not realized in MCBR-RAG; the paper only describes, in a footnote, how an application like DS-Agent could retain cases that improve test-set performance).
failure_experience_usage: Success-oriented context. Cases carry a result R (e.g., R=24 if correct for Math-24; a binary accuracy flag for Backgammon), but the framework retrieves similar cases regardless and relies on them being valid expert/solved cases; failed/negative trajectories are not specifically stored or contrastively retrieved. The experiments analyze the LLM's behavior under correct vs incorrect retrieved context (Faithfulness vs Negative Rejection) but do not maintain a failure memory.
memory_evolution_update: None -- the repository is static at runtime; stored cases are never mutated, merged, delta-updated, refined, or pruned during deployment (the only pruning -- discarding illegal Backgammon positions -- occurs once during offline construction).
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No -- retrieval is fixed similarity top-k (kNN cosine over learned latent embeddings) with hand-tuned component/objective weights. Case selection is not an RL/learned policy; while the latent encoders are trained (supervised proxy tasks), the selection rule itself is fixed arg-top_k similarity, not a trained retrieval policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No -- single-system private case repository; no multi-agent or cross-framework experience sharing.
benchmarks: Two self-constructed CBR applications: (1) Math-24 -- 466 puzzles (from 1362 solvable, restricted to (x1 o x2)x(x3 o x4)=24 form); text-generation CNN trained on 40,000 synthetic card images; 10 runs each holding out 30 test cases. (2) Backgammon -- 1015 cases collected from three expert books (Magriel; Robertie; Trice); landmark-CNN trained on 100,000 simulated board images; GNU Backgammon value-labeled dataset used for the latent value head; 10 runs each holding out 30 test cases. No standard public benchmark is used.
benchmark_family: Other / bespoke multimodal-CBR tasks (not in the standard QA/multi-hop/web/embodied/tool/code/memory/decision-RL families). Math-24 is an arithmetic-reasoning puzzle benchmark; Backgammon is a game-analysis text-generation benchmark. Both are author-constructed multimodal (text+image) case repositories.
baselines: Primary baseline: No Context (NC) -- the LLM solves/analyzes with no retrieved context (parametric-only). Math-24 also includes a General Context (GC) baseline (a fixed generic execution tip instead of a retrieved case). The proposed conditions are Top Context (TC, Math-24, k=1 retrieved case as plan) and With Context (WC, Backgammon, top-3 retrieved cases). Retrieval baselines: 'Features' (Math-24 hand-crafted feature cosine) and 'Encoding'/'Latent(0,1)' (Backgammon raw-encoding / decoder-only latent) vs the learned 'Latent' similarity. Six LLMs are evaluated as the frozen generator: Llama-3.1-405B-Instruct-Turbo, Qwen2-72B-Instruct, Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct-Turbo, Llama-3-70b-chat-hf, Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-Turbo. No external system baselines (e.g., a competing CBR/RAG method) are compared.
key_metrics: Retrieval: Precision@k, Recall@k, F1-Score@k, NDCG@k, MRR@k (averaged over k in {1..5}), reported as percentages. Generation (Math-24): Accuracy (final expression evaluates to 24 using all 4 numbers), plus Faithfulness (correct given context contains >=1 correct solution) and Negative Rejection (correct given context contains no correct solution). Generation (Backgammon): BERTScore-F1 plus sentence-transformer cosine similarity to the reference expert analysis using all-mpnet-base-v2 (MPNet), all-roberta-large-v1 (RoBERTa), all-MiniLM-L12-v1 (MiniLM), and their average (Avg).
headline_result: MCBR-RAG context consistently improves generation over the no-context baseline. Math-24: Top Context (TC, retrieved-case-as-plan) yields the highest accuracy for every LLM -- e.g., Llama-3.1-405B-Instruct-Turbo 61.3% TC vs 34.0% NC (and 30.0% GC); Qwen2-72B-Instruct 47.3% TC vs 16.7% NC (a +30.6% absolute gain over NC and +25.3% over GC). Backgammon: With Context (WC, top-3 cases) improves the average sentence-transformer score for all LLMs -- best LLM Meta-Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct-Turbo reaches 63.8% Avg with context vs 58.3% without. Retrieval: learned latent similarity beats raw-feature similarity (e.g., Math-24 SCD NDCG 65.1% latent vs 46.5% features; Backgammon best Latent(1,0.01) NDCG 45.6% vs Encoding 36.6%).
ablations: (1) Retrieval representation -- learned Latent similarity > raw Features (Math-24: SCO Latent 82.0%/SCD Latent 64.2% precision vs Features 71.9%/45.4%; SCD NDCG 65.1% vs 46.5%) and > raw Encoding (Backgammon). (2) Backgammon latent objective weighting -- sweeping (value, decoder) weights: Latent(1,0) value-only (NDCG 45.5%) >> Latent(0,1) decoder-only (NDCG 38.0%) ~ raw Encoding (36.6%), showing value is a stronger similarity signal than checker configuration; combined Latent(1,0.01) is best (NDCG 45.6%, MRR 54.2%) and is used for generation. (3) Math-24 labeling schemes -- SCO (solution-category-only) vs SCD (category+decomposition): SCD lowers precision but raises recall. (4) Query-type ablation -- TC > GC > NC for accuracy in most models, but GC does not consistently beat NC (e.g., Llama-3.1-405B NC 34.0% > GC 30.0%), indicating generic context can cause fixation. (5) Faithfulness >> Negative Rejection across all LLMs (e.g., Llama-3.1-70B 56.2% vs 18.8%), showing the LLM follows correct context well but cannot recover from incorrect context. (6) Metric ablation -- BERTScore improves inconsistently with context while all three sentence-transformer metrics improve consistently, with qualitative examples (Appendix C) showing BERTScore can be high yet semantically wrong.
evaluation_decoupling: Yes -- intrinsic retrieval metrics (Precision/Recall/F1/NDCG/MRR@k, Tables 1 and 3) are reported and analyzed separately from end-to-end generation metrics (accuracy/faithfulness/negative-rejection for Math-24, Table 2; BERTScore + sentence-transformer similarities for Backgammon, Table 4). The best retrieval configuration is selected from the intrinsic metrics before the generation experiments.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Mixed. Math-24 has a verifiable outcome metric (Accuracy: does the expression equal 24 using all four numbers) plus process-flavored diagnostics (Faithfulness / Negative Rejection conditioned on retrieved-context correctness). Backgammon has no verifiable outcome (move quality is not auto-graded); generation quality is proxied by semantic similarity to the reference expert analysis (sentence-transformer cosine), with qualitative examples arguing this captures strategic-concept match better than token-level BERTScore. No step-wise reasoning-faithfulness metric.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Not quantified in cost/latency/token terms. Overheads include training the application-specific CNN text-generators (Math-24 CNN reaches 100% test accuracy on 10,000 cards; Backgammon two CNNs over 100,000 simulated images with ~90% case-retention) and the FFNN latent models, plus one kNN retrieval and one augmented LLM call per case. No API-cost, latency, speedup, or token-count numbers are reported. The accuracy gains (e.g., Math-24 +30.6% absolute for Qwen2-72B) come at the cost of building bespoke per-application text/latent models.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k. Math-24 generation injects the single Top Context case (k=1) reformatted as an execution plan (or one generic tip for GC). Backgammon generation injects the top-3 (k=3) most similar cases (position JSON + player + dice + move + expert analysis each). Retrieval metrics are averaged over k in {1,2,3,4,5}. No explicit token budget, budget-cap, or reranked-then-truncated selection is reported.
benchmark_construction_and_size: Both repositories are author-constructed. Math-24: 466 cases (subset of the 1362 solvable puzzles, restricted to solutions of form (x1 o x2)x(x3 o x4)=24); supporting CNN trained on 40,000 synthetic card images (4 random numbers 1-13), reaching 100% test accuracy on 10,000 held-out cards; answers are verifiable (expression must equal 24 using all four numbers). Backgammon: 1015 cases reverse-engineered from three expert books by OCR/CNN extraction of board images (landmark CNN trained on 100,000 simulated boards; part CNN predicts checker count/owner; ~90% case-retention after legality validation), with value labels from the public GNU Backgammon training dataset; answers are free-text expert analyses (not exactly verifiable -- scored by semantic similarity). Difficulty signal: best Math-24 accuracy 61.3% (Llama-3.1-405B TC); Backgammon best Avg similarity 63.8% with context. Cases are labeled for retrieval relevance via solution category/decomposition (Math-24) or grouped book chapter names (~75% of Backgammon cases labelable).
builds_on: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (Lewis et al., NeurIPS 2020); the CBR cycle / case-based decision theory (Aamodt & Plaza 1994; Gilboa & Schmeidler 1995); prior LLM+RAG-for-CBR works -- CBR-RAG (Wiratunga et al., ICCBR 2024), CaseGPT (Yang 2024), DS-Agent (Guo et al., ICML 2024), CBR for logical-fallacy classification (Sourati et al., IJCAI 2023); multimodal RAG -- retrieval-augmented multimodal LM (Yasunaga et al., ICML 2023), BLIP-2 (Li et al., ICML 2023), RECAP audio captioning (Ghosh et al. 2023), retrieval-augmented egocentric video captioning (Xu et al., CVPR 2024); transformer encoders BERT (Devlin et al. 2019) and GPT-2 (Radford et al. 2019); TD-Gammon position encoding (Tesauro 1995) and GNU Backgammon value data; sentence-transformer / scoring models MPNet, RoBERTa, MiniLM, BERTScore; Dense Passage Retrieval (Karpukhin et al., EMNLP 2020) for the relevance-vs-recall argument.
contrasts_with: No Context (LLM parametric-only generation) -- the primary comparator; General Context (Math-24 generic fixed tip, shown to be unreliable / sometimes worse than NC); raw-feature / raw-encoding retrieval similarity (vs the learned latent similarity); token-level evaluation (BERTScore, criticized as rewarding jargon overlap) vs semantic sentence-transformer similarity. Positioned against prior CBR-RAG works (CBR-RAG, CaseGPT, DS-Agent, logical-fallacy CBR) that are TEXT-ONLY, whereas MCBR-RAG generalizes the Retrieve+Reuse RAG-for-CBR recipe to MULTIMODAL cases via application-specific text-generation and latent-representation functions.
lineage: Group D (case-based planning / case-based reasoning lineage). Directly extends the CBR-RAG line (Wiratunga et al. 2024) to the multimodal setting: it abstracts the Retrieve (RAG retrieval) + Reuse (RAG generation) recipe and adds per-component text-generation and learned latent-representation functions so non-text case components can be indexed and injected. Sits alongside CaseGPT and DS-Agent in the LLM-RAG-for-CBR sub-lineage, distinguished by (a) explicit multimodal-case formalization, (b) weighted per-component latent retrieval, and (c) leaving Revise/Retain application-specific.
